q1_issues.issue: `During` is used for the surface preposition "in" ("in Thursday morning trading"); the instruction set states the head must be the preposition actually used and that `During` renders only the word "during".
no kind/type atom for `nasdaq_stock_market` — the naming rule requires the entity's kind be stated in an ordinary type atom whether the kind word sits inside the name or beside it.
`(Measure sk_shares_1 price 27.43 dollar)` puts a per-share price on a group symbol, where the instruction set reads a measure on a plural as the group AGGREGATE (it does not distribute).
`(Measure sk_rise_1 price 4 dollar)` predicates a price of the rise EVENT rather than recording a delta; the $4 is the size of the change, not the event's price.
a second `Measure` on the same entity and the same `price` scale (17.2 percent) collides with statement 6 — the two are the same delta restated by an appositive "or", not two independent measures.

q2_gaps: a measured delta on a scalar-change verb ("rose $4", "to $27.43") — `MoreBy` is comparative-only and `BeforeBy` temporal-only, so neither the increment nor the resulting value has a licensed encoding
reformulative/appositive "or" ("$4, or 17.2 percent") that restates one quantity in another unit rather than disjoining — treating it as `(Or ...)` would be wrong and nothing else is offered

a proper-noun modifier on a common noun ("Allegiant shares") — neither the multi-word-name rule (whole NP is a name) nor the possessor/part "car engine" rule squarely covers a company name naming the issuer
notes: Source text is defective ("$17.2 percent" mixes a currency sign with a percentage). `(Possession sk_shares_1 allegiant)` is a defensible opaque reading of "Allegiant shares" given the gap above.
